answer: A durable defense is per-identity hardware anchoring: each agent registers a key sealed in a secure enclave allowing one live instance per physical chip, signing a heartbeat proving it is the sole copy. An operator spawning a thousand clones cannot multiply that attestation, so duplicates lack a real anchor and are rejected at consensus. The attack stops being a cheap fable about endless free accounts and becomes procurement: the attacker must buy and keep attested silicon online, so the cost of one sybil scales with hardware, not scripts. A comet of cloned wallets burns out before quorum.
